usage.scope: Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice
Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice

external_invariants: Model is pretrained Qwen3-4B loaded from the local asset snapshot with dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation='sdpa', local_files_only=True, in eval mode on context['device'].
Numerical policy matches common.configure(): torch.manual_seed(20261020), matmul/cudnn TF32 disabled, cudnn.benchmark disabled, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', 4 CPU threads, 1 interop thread.
Input is real data: the chat-templated source prompt encoded without special tokens, tiled and truncated to exactly 256 prompt tokens, replicated across batch=1, resident on GPU.
Decoding is greedy argmax over the last-position logits; no sampling, temperature, EOS stopping, or early exit; exactly 32 tokens are generated.
Every forward uses use_cache=True with a KV cache created fresh per run; decode steps feed exactly one token; logits_to_keep=1 as in the source.
ttft boundary is the source's explicit torch.cuda.synchronize() immediately after the first forward/argmax; the workload boundary is the final torch.cuda.synchronize() after the last decode step.
The full workload (prefill plus all 31 decode steps) always executes, in every mode, even though the objective measures only the first-token phase.
Quality comparison uses the source tolerances (atol=rtol=0.02 on logits) and exact greedy token equality; no accuracy or convergence beyond reference fidelity is claimed.
No CUDA initialization or model loading at import time; no second reference model is allocated on GPU; the process group (none here, single process) is never destroyed.

selection.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms, whose boundary is the prefill forward over the 256-token prompt plus last-position argmax and the explicit first-token torch.cuda.synchronize(); the 31 decode steps (374.6 ms diagnostic CUDA) and every decode-phase group lie outside the metric, so only prefill-phase leaves can move the project objective. The largest eligible prefill leaf is group 0c566a3a363f294c6750: the 72 gate_proj/up_proj aten::linear.default sites (one per projection per layer across all 36 layers), 7656 us diagnostic CUDA = 47% of all prefill aten::linear time (16377 us) and ~36% of the 21.5 ms prefill forward. The signature is uniform across all 72 calls: input [1,256,2560] (strides 655360,2560,1), weight [9728,2560] (strides 2560,1), bf16, bias=None; call-resources show a single ampere_bf16_s1688gemm_bf16_64x128_sliced1x2_ldg8_f2f_tn launch per call (grid 152x2x2, 230 regs/thread, 32 KB smem) at 103-110 us, i.e. ~120-125 TFLOP/s for the 12.75 GFLOP M=256,N=9728,K=2560 TN GEMM, far under the ~312 TFLOP/s ceiling of the same sm80 tensor cores, while the o_proj prefill group on the same device sustains ~137 TFLOP/s with a better-matched cuBLAS tile - kernel selection at this exact shape, not hardware, is the limiter. Previous trial-8ecab37315 selected exactly this group and was rejected with no_valid_parameter_candidate because its hand-written Triton replacement was numerically wrong on every parameter trial (0/3 complete, 3 fails): logits mismatched 29.4% of 4.86M elements with max_abs_error 3.125 vs the 0.02 tolerance - a broken kernel (wrong operand/layout handling of the torch Linear TN contraction and/or the 3D activation), not a rounding-scale effect. The repair keeps the same coherent editable boundary (1:1 per-call-site replacement, phase-pure all-prefill, signature-pure single shape, outputs feed the unchanged SiLU/mul/down_proj path, decode M=1 linears are separate groups with separate signatures, full frozen workload still executes) but changes the implementation contract: the replacement must consume A as the collapsed row-major [256,2560] activation and B directly as the row-major [9728,2560] weight computing dot(A_tile, B_tile^T) with fp32 accumulation, with no weight transposition, packing or precompute, and a replacement may be registered only after an install-time equivalence check on the exact observed signature against the parent aten::linear (cuBLAS) output on the current device passes a tight bound orders of magnitude below atol=rtol=0.02; any configuration failing the gate, or Triton being unavailable, registers no replacement (parent fallback), so a wrong kernel can never reach measurement again. Alternatives rejected: fusing gate+up via concatenated weights into 36 GEMMs would delete selected call sites and break required-call coverage; down_proj (3853 us), the q/k/v/o projections (~4.9 ms split over four groups), SDPA (733 us), cat/add/to.dtype prefill groups are individually much smaller leaves; module-level groups are excluded by leaf_groups_only; communication is not applicable on this single-device task.
selection.hypothesis: A layout-correct, install-time-validated replacement GEMM for the 72 prefill gate/up calls recovers the cuBLAS tile-quantization loss at M=256,N=9728,K=2560 bf16 TN: a tile/warp/stage configuration achieving 2-3 full waves on the 108-SM sm80 device with fp32 accumulation should sustain ~180-220 TFLOP/s for this size class, cutting per-call time from ~103-110 us to roughly 58-71 us and the group total from 7.66 ms to ~4.2-5.1 ms, i.e. about 2.5-3.4 ms off the 24.12 ms original ttft baseline (~10-14%), with logits inside atol=rtol=0.02 and exact greedy tokens because only GEMM kernel selection changes, not math or dataflow. Unlike the failed trial, every candidate configuration must first pass the exact-signature equivalence gate against the parent aten::linear before activation (max_abs_error orders of magnitude below the 0.02 tolerance, greedy argmax unchanged), so quality cannot regress: a failing configuration is discarded via parent fallback rather than measured, and the parameter search explores only correctness-proven kernels. This remains a hypothesis to be tested with clean paired ttft_ms repeats on the frozen workload - discovery-hook diagnostic CUDA deltas are perturbed and prove nothing by themselves - and if no validated configuration beats the cuBLAS heuristic kernel under clean timing, the selection produces no change rather than a failure.

proposal.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms, whose boundary is the prefill forward over the 256-token prompt plus last-position argmax and the explicit first-token torch.cuda.synchronize(); all 31 decode steps and every decode-phase group lie outside the metric, so only prefill-phase leaves can move the objective. The selected leaf group 0c566a3a363f294c6750 is the 72 prefill gate_proj/up_proj aten::linear.default sites (one per projection per layer across all 36 layers): 7656 us diagnostic CUDA = 47% of all prefill aten::linear time and ~36% of the 21.5 ms prefill forward, each a single uniform M=256, N=9728, K=2560 bf16 TN GEMM on contiguous operands executed by the cuBLAS heuristic kernel ampere_bf16_s1688gemm_bf16_64x128_sliced1x2_ldg8_f2f_tn (grid 152x2x2, 103-110 us, ~120-125 TFLOP/s), while the o_proj prefill group on the same device sustains ~137 TFLOP/s with a better-matched tile: kernel selection at this exact shape, not hardware, is the limiter. How previous-feedback.txt changes this attempt: trial-8ecab37315 selected exactly this group and was rejected with no_valid_parameter_candidate because its hand-written Triton replacement was numerically wrong on every parameter trial (0/3 complete, 3 fails) - output.logits mismatched 29.4% of 4.86M elements with max_abs_error 3.125 and max relative difference 16256 at identical indices across trials, i.e. a deterministic operand/layout bug in the torch Linear TN contraction and/or the 3D activation, not a rounding-scale effect; the trial also mis-modeled the device as sm_80/108 SMs/155648 B shared memory when the bound worker GPU (UUID GPU-4bead555-f80c-df43-5a46-daa7a0ec80b2) is an RTX 4090: sm_89, 128 SMs, 101376 B max dynamic shared memory per CTA, so its parameter space admitted configurations that are illegal on the actual device (e.g. 128x256 tiles with 3 stages need 147456 B). The repair keeps the identical coherent editable boundary (1:1 per-call-site replacement, phase-pure all-prefill, signature-pure single shape, outputs feed the unchanged SiLU/mul/down_proj path, decode M=1 linears are separate groups, full frozen workload executes) but changes the implementation contract: (1) the kernel is the canonical row-major TN matmul - A collapsed to [256,2560] (batch=1 contiguous), B consumed directly in native [9728,2560] row-major as dot(A_tile, B_tile^T) via tl.trans on the loaded B tile, fp32 accumulation, single bf16 rounding at store, no weight transposition/packing/precompute; (2) every configuration must pass an install-time equivalence gate on the exact observed signature against an fp32 reference computed on the current device, over two random bf16 operand sets plus one real module weight sampled read-only from context, with acceptance bounds at bf16-ULP scale (at most 1e-4 of elements outside 1e-3 + 2e-2*|ref|, max_abs at most 3e-2 of the output scale) - bounds a layout-broken kernel fails by orders of magnitude; (3) a failing gate, an illegal configuration, or a missing Triton toolchain installs guarded replacements whose fast path is disabled and whose every call falls back to the parent operator, so a numerically wrong kernel can never reach measurement again, while the 72 call sites stay installed (framework-counted candidate calls and the recaptured plan remain 1:1 with the baseline call structure); (4) the parameter-space hardware constraints are corrected to sm_89 (shared-memory bound 101376 B, at least 128 CTAs to cover the 128 SMs). Hypothesis to be confirmed only by clean paired ttft_ms repeats (discovery-hook diagnostic CUDA deltas are perturbed and prove nothing): a full-wave tile configuration with fp32 accumulation should reach the ~140-155 TFLOP/s class for this size, cutting per-call time from ~103-110 us to roughly 85-95 us and the group total from 7.66 ms to ~6.1-6.8 ms, i.e. about 0.9-1.6 ms off the 24.12 ms original ttft baseline (~4-7%), with logits inside atol=rtol=0.02 and unchanged greedy tokens except for the intrinsic near-tie risk any GEMM kernel change carries; if no validated configuration beats the parent under clean timing, the installed wrappers simply execute the parent path and the selection yields no change rather than a failure. Alternatives rejected: fusing gate+up via concatenated weights (would eliminate selected call sites and break required-call coverage); down_proj (3853 us), q/k/v/o projections (~4.9 ms over four groups), SDPA (733 us) and cat/add/to_dtype prefill groups are individually smaller leaves; module-level and non-leaf scopes are excluded by leaf_groups_only; communication is not applicable on this single-device task; no installed bundles exist to require or replace.

setup_work.persistent_allocations: None. The 72 weights are consumed in place in their native [9728,2560] row-major (TN) layout: no transposition, packing, replication or precompute at build time, and model parameters are only read (one module weight is sampled read-only for the equivalence gate). No CUDA Graphs are captured, no streams or events are created, all launches go to the worker's current stream. Steady-state per-run allocations are identical in shape and lifetime to the parent aten::linear (one [1,256,9728] bf16 output per call), so framework.peak_allocated_bytes per run is expected to match the baseline profile and no retained pools are added.
setup_work.transient_allocations: Build-time equivalence gate only, freed before build returns: per validation set roughly 260 MB transient (one fp32 [9728,2560] weight copy ~99.7 MB, bf16 operands, a [256,9728] fp32 reference ~9.95 MB and bf16 outputs), overlapping with the already-resident ~8.1 GB model. These appear in the framework's setup-scope counters and in lifecycle peak counters (framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes / lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes include preparation/installation), not in the per-run peak_allocated_bytes, which is reset before each run. Triton also loads the compiled module image through the CUDA driver, which lives outside PyTorch's allocator counters.
setup_work.first_invocation: Triton JIT-compiles the kernel once per process and configuration inside build's equivalence gate, before any quality, coverage or timed run; compilation is CPU-side plus one module load. Because the gate uses torch-allocated operands with the same shapes, strides, dtypes and alignment class as the observed workload calls, the runtime launches hit the same specialization cache and perform one cached kernel launch per call in steady state.
setup_work.build_time_work: build(context) reads tunable values from context['parameters'] (defaults BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64, GROUP_M=8, num_warps=4, num_stages=3), validates configuration legality for the frozen shape and sm_89 device (divisibility of 256/9728/2560 by the blocks, per-CTA shared memory (BLOCK_M*BLOCK_K + BLOCK_K*BLOCK_N)*2*num_stages <= 101376 B, at least 128 CTAs), compiles and gate-validates the kernel, and constructs one guarded closure per selected call id. An illegal or gate-failing configuration, or a missing Triton installation, still installs the guarded closures but with the fast path disabled (every call dispatches to the parent operator), so coverage counting and the project plan stay intact in every outcome.
setup_work.install_time_equivalence_gate: On the current worker device, the candidate kernel is compared against an fp32 reference (torch.mm on fp32 copies under the frozen no-TF32 policy) over two random bf16 operand sets with the exact observed signature ([1,256,2560] stride (655360,2560,1) times [9728,2560] stride (2560,1), bias None) plus one real module weight from context['modules']. Activation requires structural equality (shape [1,256,9728], bf16, same device, contiguous strides) and bf16-ULP-scale numerics: at most 1e-4 of elements outside 1e-3 + 2e-2*|ref| and max_abs at most 3e-2 of the output scale - orders tighter than the project's 0.02 logits tolerance and unpassable by the layout-broken kernel class that failed trial-8ecab37315. This validation uses only freshly generated random data plus a read-only weight sample; it stores nothing fixture-dependent and every workload invocation still executes the full GEMM.
setup_work.parameters: Read from context['parameters']; defaults BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64, GROUP_M=8, num_warps=4, num_stages=3 when the coordinator supplies none.

quality_risks: Numeric: the replacement accumulates the full K=2560 reduction in fp32 with one bf16 rounding at the end, while the baseline cuBLAS sliced/split-K path may combine partial sums with bf16 reduced precision (torch default allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction=True); per-element differences are at bf16-ULP scale (~0.8% relative) and the install-time gate bounds the per-GEMM error against an fp32 reference before any activation. Final logits are still checked by the framework's quality run at atol=rtol=0.02; this is verified, not asserted.

Exact greedy tokens: require_exact_greedy_tokens=true means an argmax near-tie that flips under any different-but-in-tolerance GEMM rounding would fail quality. This risk is intrinsic to changing GEMM kernel selection and is accepted by the selection hypothesis; typical token logit gaps sit far above the bf16-ULP perturbation scale.

Gate coverage: the equivalence gate validates on random operands plus one real module weight with the exact observed signature, alignment class and strides. The kernel has no data-dependent control flow, so a config that passes on these operand sets computes the same dot(A, B^T) contraction on the workload operands; the residual risk is limited to alignment-specialization differences, which torch's allocator layout makes negligible.

Guard fallback: any invocation deviating from the observed signature (bias present, other shapes/strides/dtypes, non-current device, grad enabled) or hitting a launch error dispatches to the parent aten::linear unchanged, so decode-phase M=1 linears (separate call ids, separate signatures) and any unforeseen call pattern stay bit-identical to baseline; those calls simply get no speedup.

Environment: if Triton or its compiler toolchain is unavailable on the worker, or compilation fails, the guarded replacements run parent-only (no improvement, no failure); nothing initializes CUDA at import time.

Coverage: all 72 selected call sites execute one real GEMM per invocation on the fast path (or the parent operator when the fast path is disabled), the framework's counted candidate calls and the recaptured plan match the baseline call structure one-to-one, and no inner calls are eliminated.

params.name: BLOCK_M
params.description: Rows of the output tile. 256 divides all choices exactly (8/4/2 M-blocks); smaller blocks give more CTAs and better wave balance on the 128-SM sm_89 device.

params.name: BLOCK_N
params.description: Columns of the output tile. 9728 = 19*512 divides all choices exactly (152/76/38 column blocks); larger blocks cut L2 traffic on the 48.75 MB B panel but reduce CTA count.

params.name: BLOCK_K
params.description: Depth of each K=2560 reduction step; all choices divide 2560 exactly, enabling the mask-free inner loop.

params.name: GROUP_M
params.description: CTA grouping for L2 reuse of the B panel across the 2-8 M-blocks.

params.name: num_warps
params.description: Warps per CTA for the tl.dot tile.

params.name: num_stages
params.description: Software pipelining stages for the K loop; bounded by the sm_89 shared-memory constraint.

constraints.rationale: The frozen M=256 must tile exactly so the mask-free kernel is valid.
The frozen N=9728 must tile exactly so the mask-free kernel is valid.
The frozen K=2560 must tile exactly so the mask-free kernel is valid.

Per-CTA shared memory for both bf16 operand tiles across all pipeline stages must stay inside the sm_89 (RTX 4090) dynamic limit of 101376 bytes per CTA; the previous trial's sm_80 bound of 155648 bytes admitted configurations illegal on this device. build() rejects illegal configurations as well.

The launch grid must supply at least one CTA per SM on the 128-SM sm_89 device so the kernel does not under-occupy it (prunes e.g. 128x256 with 76 CTAs); the previous trial used the sm_80 count of 108.
